notes.meaning: God responds to people according to their hearts and actions. To those who are honest and pure, He proves Himself completely faithful and true. But when someone chooses a twisted and crooked path, God outmatches their cunning and turns their schemes upside down.

The Lord delivers humble and suffering people who call out to Him. At the same time, He pulls down the proud who look down on others with arrogant eyes. God defends the weak and opposes those who rely on their own conceited strength.

The Lord keeps David's life bright and full of hope, like a glowing household lamp. When dark seasons of grief and danger close in, God shines His presence to drive away the gloom. Believers can trust God to bring comfort when life feels overwhelming.

God gives David the courage and power to break through an entire troop of armed enemies. With the Lord helping him, he can even leap over fortified city walls during battle. He gives all credit for his daring victories to God rather than his own skill.

Everything God does is perfect, wise, and completely without error. His promises are like pure gold that has passed through fire without failing a single test. He covers and protects like a sturdy shield anyone who runs to Him for safety.

The Lord alone is the true God, and no helpless idol can take His place. He is the only solid rock in the universe where a person can stand without shaking. Because He has no rivals, His people can place their full trust in Him.

God equips David with strength just like a soldier strapping on a tight belt before running into battle. The Lord clears away every hidden trap and makes his march smooth and successful. Every bit of strength David uses comes directly from God's hand.

The Lord makes David as swift and sure-footed as a wild mountain deer. He places him safely upon high rocky peaks where his enemies cannot reach him. God gives His servants both the speed to pursue duty and the safety to stand firm.

David recognizes that God personally trained his hands and muscles for the demands of war. With the Lord's help, his arms can bend even a stiff bow made of solid bronze. Natural abilities and acquired skills are both gifts from the Lord.

God protects David in every battle by holding out His own saving power as a protective shield. His strong right hand keeps the king from stumbling into deadly traps. David's honor came not from his own greatness, but from God stooping down in kindness to lift him up.

differ.view: Translates the word as God humbling David so that through lowliness he is made great.
Understands the phrase as God's loving correction and fatherly discipline that trains and elevates the king.
Emphasizes that God's gentleness teaches believers humility and patience, which leads to true honor.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate renders this statement as God's discipline teaching and guiding the king toward greatness.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern translators understand the phrase to mean God's favorable answer or willingness to respond to prayer.

notes.meaning: The Lord widens the narrow, rocky paths beneath David so his feet have plenty of room to step. This broad path keeps his ankles steady so he does not slip or fall in dangerous places. God leads His people out of tight distress into safe and open spaces.

Guided and strengthened by God, David chased down his enemies and overtook them in the field. He did not quit or turn back until the opposing forces were entirely defeated. He acted with complete focus as God's appointed leader executing justice.

David struck down his opponents so thoroughly that they could not get back up to fight. They fell helpless on the ground beneath his feet. The Lord granted him complete victory over every army that tried to destroy him.

God provided David with internal courage and physical power for the contest. The Lord Himself forced those who rebelled against David to bow beneath his authority. True spiritual and earthly victories belong entirely to God's power.

The Lord made David's enemies turn their backs and run away in retreat. Having their backs and necks turned showed that they were totally scattered and defeated. David was able to put an end to those who hated him and resisted God's rule.

The fleeing enemies cried out desperately for rescue, but no helper appeared. In their terror they even called upon the Lord, but He refused to answer their cries. God will not listen to insincere cries from people who hate His righteousness and harm His people.

David ground his enemies down until they were scattered like fine dust before the wind. He stamped them out and swept them away like useless mud in the streets. Their military power and pride were completely wiped out by God's judgment.

God rescued David from civil wars and rebellions among his own people. Then the Lord promoted him to rule over neighboring lands and nations far beyond Israel's borders. People he had never met before began to serve him and pay him tribute.

Foreign nations surrendered as soon as reports of David's mighty deeds reached their ears. Strangers came cowering before him, submitting quickly out of awe and fear. Even without seeing him face to face, they yielded to his authority.

Foreign enemies lost their courage and withered away like dried-up leaves in autumn. They came trembling out of their secret hideouts and high stone forts to surrender. No fortress can keep an enemy safe when God decides to bring them down.

David rejoices because the Lord is alive, unlike the dead and powerless idols of the nations. He blesses God as his strong, unchanging Rock and praises Him for his rescue. The living God deserves joyful and public praise from all His people.

God took up David's cause, bringing justice on his enemies and subduing nations beneath his feet. David did not take personal revenge into his own hands, but trusted the Lord to make things right. The Lord is the defender of those who walk faithfully with Him.

The Lord pulled David safely out of the grip of his foes and lifted him high above his attackers. He rescued him from violent men, including King Saul who had hunted him for years. God has the power to keep His servants safe against the cruelest opposition.

David vows to sing praises to God openly among the foreign nations. Because God's fame spread through these victories, the surrounding peoples learned about the true Lord. The apostle Paul pointed to this verse to show that God always intended to bring Gentile nations to praise Him through Christ.

differ.view: Believe that Paul applies the verse to the Gentiles praising God, but that David's original intention was simply his own praise among the nations he conquered.
Believe David spoke as an inspired type of Christ, so the verse was designed as a direct prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles.

notes.meaning: God gives wonderful deliverances to the king He chooses, showing unending, loyal love to David and his family line forever. While this applied to David's kingdom, it points forward to Jesus Christ, David's greatest descendant. In Christ, God's people share in a victory that will never end.
